web.title: Embed Images using CID - Resend
web.description:
# Embed Images using CID Learn how to inline image attachments in your emails. Today, we're announcing support for inline image attachments using `CID` (or Content-ID). Inlining an image embeds the image itself in the email (instead of hosting it somewhere else) and shows it inside the email body instead of as an attachment. ## [How to embed images](https://resend.com/changelog/embed-images-using-cid#how-to-embed-images) ### [2. Reference the CID in the attachment](https://resend.com/changelog/embed-images-using-cid#2-reference-the-cid-in-the-attachment) ``` "attachments": [\ {\ "path": "https://resend.com/static/sample/logo.png",\ "filename": "logo.png",\ "content_id": "logo-image"\ }\ ] ``` ## [How it works](https://resend.com/changelog/embed-images-using-cid#how-it-works) As with all our features, inline images are available across all our SDKs. [All attachment requirements, options, and limitations](https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/emails/attachments) apply to inline images as well. Both remote and local attachments are supported, but here is an example of inlining remote images. ``` await resend.emails.send({ from: 'Acme ', to: ['delivered@resend.dev'], subject: 'Thank you for contacting us', html: '

Here is our inline logo

', attachments: [\ {\ path: 'https://resend.com/static/sample/logo.png',\ filename: 'logo.png',\ \ contentId: 'logo-image',\ },\ ], }); ``` ## [Other considerations](https://resend.com/changelog/embed-images-using-cid#other-considerations) - Inline images increase the size of the email.

web.title: CID Attachment Email: Embed Images Without URLs
web.description:
# CID Attachment Email: What It Is and How It Works
## Content-Disposition: inline vs. attachment
```
Content-Type: image/png; name="logo.png"
Content-Disposition: inline; filename="logo.png"
Content-ID: <logo@example.com>
Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64
```

## Key Takeaways
- The image MIME part must carry `Content-Disposition: inline`; setting it to `attachment` breaks inline rendering even with a valid `cid:` reference.
- CID outperforms base64 inline embedding on message size and Outlook compatibility. Base64 inline is blocked entirely in Outlook and increases payload size.
